fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. In the dream, the thin cows don't run from anybody. Genesis 41:4 says the sickly, thin cows “…devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.” The skinny ones come up from the Nile and eat the fat ones. Cows eating cows? That is NOT how cows work, and I'd say that's the whole point of the dream.

Rested sounds lovely, friend, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, did fall back asleep between the dreams (Genesis 41:5). But two dreams of skinny things eating fat things is not a recipe for a good morning. The text says “In the morning his spirit was troubled…” (Genesis 41:8). That's a man who needed a second cup of nothing, because he got no rest at all. So he summons the magicians and wise men of Egypt.

Good thinking, friend, because the captain of the guard does show up later! The cupbearer says the young Hebrew was a servant of the captain of the guard (Genesis 41:12). But that's later in the story, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, isn't calling him yet. In Genesis 41:8 he summons “…all the magicians and wise men of Egypt.” Right name from the passage, wrong spot on the guest list.

problems.problem: “I’d have been reaching for the nearest pillow too” implies Pharaoh reached for a pillow, which the text does not say.
The explanation is flat and mostly repeats the distinction between rested and troubled without much of Papa Dorin’s personality.
The explanation is a plain factual correction, with little of Papa Dorin’s warmth or humor.
